# googleplay_subscription_offer (Resource)

A subscription offer: a free trial, an introductory price or a discount on one base plan of a subscription, for the users its targeting picks.

An offer has its own create and update calls, so unlike a base plan it is a resource of its own. Only auto-renewing base plans can have offers. An offer runs through one or two phases, in order, before the user pays the base plan price: a free trial, a single payment, or a number of discounted recurring payments.

~> **What Google Play does not let you undo.** An offer can be deleted only while it is a draft. Destroying one that has been activated deactivates it, removes it from state with a warning, and leaves it in Play Console. Play Console's help says an offer id cannot be reused, even after the offer is deleted.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A week's free trial, then three months at half price, for users who have
# never subscribed to anything in the app. The offer belongs to the monthly
# base plan of the subscription `pro_monthly`.
resource "googleplay_subscription_offer" "pro_monthly_intro" {
  package_name = "com.example.app"
  product_id   = "pro_monthly"
  base_plan_id = "monthly"
  offer_id     = "intro"

  # A new offer is a draft until its state says otherwise.
  state = "ACTIVE"

  # The regions the offer is set up in. Every phase prices each of them.
  regional_configs = {
    US = { new_subscriber_availability = true }
    GB = { new_subscriber_availability = true }
  }

  other_regions_config = {
    new_subscriber_availability = true
  }

  phases = [
    {
      duration         = "P1W"
      recurrence_count = 1
      regional_configs = {
        US = { free = {} }
        GB = { free = {} }
      }
      other_regions_config = { free = {} }
    },
    {
      duration         = "P1M"
      recurrence_count = 3
      regional_configs = {
        US = { relative_discount = 0.5 }
        GB = { price = { currency_code = "GBP", amount = "3.99" } }
      }
      other_regions_config = { relative_discount = 0.5 }
    },
  ]

  targeting = {
    acquisition_rule = {
      scope = { any_subscription_in_app = {} }
    }
  }

  offer_tags = ["intro"]
}

# A first month at a fixed price for users upgrading from the monthly plan of
# another subscription, once per user.
resource "googleplay_subscription_offer" "max_monthly_upgrade" {
  package_name = "com.example.app"
  product_id   = "max_monthly"
  base_plan_id = "monthly"
  offer_id     = "upgrade-from-pro"

  regional_configs = {
    US = { new_subscriber_availability = true }
  }

  phases = [{
    duration         = "P1M"
    recurrence_count = 1
    regional_configs = {
      US = { price = { currency_code = "USD", amount = "9.99" } }
    }
  }]

  targeting = {
    upgrade_rule = {
      scope                   = { specific_subscription_in_app = "pro_monthly" }
      billing_period_duration = "P1M"
      once_per_user           = true
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `base_plan_id` (String) The id of the base plan the offer belongs to. It must be an auto-renewing base plan. Changing it creates a new offer.
- `offer_id` (String) The id of the offer, unique within the base plan. Play Console's help says an offer id cannot be reused, even after the offer is deleted. Changing it creates a new offer.
- `package_name` (String) The package name (application id) of the app, for example `com.example.app`. The app must already exist in Play Console: the API cannot create one. Changing it creates a new offer.
- `phases` (Attributes List) The one or two phases of the offer, in the order the user goes through them. After the last one the user pays the base plan price. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--phases))
- `product_id` (String) The product id of the subscription the offer belongs to. Changing it creates a new offer.
- `regional_configs` (Attributes Map) The regions the offer is set up in, by region code, for example `US`. Every phase must price each of them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--regional_configs))

### Optional

- `latency_tolerance` (String) How quickly a change must reach clients: `PRODUCT_UPDATE_LATENCY_TOLERANCE_LATENCY_SENSITIVE` (within minutes; at most 7,200 updates per app per hour) or `PRODUCT_UPDATE_LATENCY_TOLERANCE_LATENCY_TOLERANT` (within 24 hours; a far higher quota). It is sent with every call that accepts it. Left out, the API uses latency-sensitive. It is a setting of the request, not of the product: changing it alone calls nothing.
- `offer_tags` (Set of String) Up to 20 custom tags for this offer, returned to the app by the billing library. Each is lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, at most 20 characters.
- `other_regions_config` (Attributes) Whether the offer is available in regions Google Play launches in later. A phase prices them with its own `other_regions_config`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--other_regions_config))
- `regions_version` (String) The version of Google Play's list of available regions that the regional prices in this configuration are written against. The API requires it on every call that creates or changes the product, and accepts an older version than the current one. Defaults to `2022/02`. Google publishes the current version in [this article](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10532353), and the `googleplay_converted_region_prices` data source reports it as `region_version`. The API does not report which version an offer was last written with, so the value is only what the configuration says.
- `state` (String) The state of the offer: `DRAFT`, `ACTIVE` or `INACTIVE`. A new offer is a draft until activated. Set `ACTIVE` to make it available and `INACTIVE` to retire it; the provider reaches the state with the `offers.activate` and `offers.deactivate` calls. A offer that has left `DRAFT` cannot return to it. Left out, the state is whatever the API reports and is never changed. The state of the base plan comes first: an active offer is not available while its base plan is not active.
- `targeting` (Attributes) Who Google Play offers this to. Set exactly one of `acquisition_rule` and `upgrade_rule`. Left out, Google Play applies no rule: the offer is developer determined, and the app decides whom to show it to. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--targeting))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `{package_name}/{product_id}/{base_plan_id}/{offer_id}`.

<a id="nestedatt--phases"></a>
### Nested Schema for `phases`

Required:

- `duration` (String) The duration of one recurrence of the phase, as an ISO 8601 duration such as `P1W` or `P1M`.
- `recurrence_count` (Number) How many times the phase repeats. Unless the phase is free, each recurrence charges its price.
- `regional_configs` (Attributes Map) What the phase costs by region code. It must have exactly one entry for each region in the offer's `regional_configs`. Set exactly one of `price`, `absolute_discount`, `relative_discount` and `free`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--phases--regional_configs))

Optional:

- `other_regions_config` (Attributes) What the phase costs in any region Google Play launches in later. Set exactly one of `price`, `absolute_discount`, `relative_discount` and `free`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--phases--other_regions_config))

<a id="nestedatt--phases--regional_configs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `phases.regional_configs`

Optional:

- `absolute_discount` (Attributes) The amount subtracted from the base plan price, prorated over the phase duration. With a base plan of 12.00 a year, a discount of 1.00 on a three-month phase makes it 2.00. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--phases--regional_configs--absolute_discount))
- `free` (Attributes) Makes the phase free: write `free = {}`. A free first phase is a free trial. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--phases--regional_configs--free))
- `price` (Attributes) The price the user pays for the phase, in the currency Google Play links to the region. It must not be below the minimum price of the region. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--phases--regional_configs--price))
- `relative_discount` (Number) The fraction of the base plan price, prorated over the phase duration, that the user pays, strictly between 0 and 1: `0.5` is half price. With a base plan of 12.00 a year, `0.5` for a three-month phase is 1.50. The result is rounded to the nearest billable unit, and must not fall below the minimum price of the region.

<a id="nestedatt--phases--regional_configs--absolute_discount"></a>
### Nested Schema for `phases.regional_configs.absolute_discount`

Required:

- `amount` (String) The amount as a decimal string, for example `"4.99"`. It is converted to the API's units and nanos exactly, never through a floating-point number, and `"4.50"` and `"4.5"` are the same amount. At most 9 fractional digits.
- `currency_code` (String) The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code, for example `USD`.

- `price` (Attributes) The price the user pays for the phase in new regions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--phases--other_regions_config--price))

With a base plan of 12.00 a year, `0.5` for a three-month phase is 1.50. The result is rounded to the nearest billable unit, and must not fall below the minimum price of the region.

<a id="nestedatt--targeting"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targeting`

Optional:

- `acquisition_rule` (Attributes) Offers it to new customers: users who have never subscribed within the scope. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--targeting--acquisition_rule))
- `upgrade_rule` (Attributes) Offers it to users who currently hold a subscription, to upgrade from it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--targeting--upgrade_rule))

<a id="nestedatt--targeting--acquisition_rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targeting.acquisition_rule`

Required:

<a id="nestedatt--targeting--acquisition_rule--scope"></a>

- `this_subscription` (Attributes) The subscription this offer belongs to: write `this_subscription = {}`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--targeting--acquisition_rule--scope--this_subscription))

<a id="nestedatt--targeting--upgrade_rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targeting.upgrade_rule`

Required:

- `scope` (Attributes) The subscription the user must currently hold. Set exactly one of `this_subscription` and `specific_subscription_in_app`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--targeting--upgrade_rule--scope))

Optional:

- `billing_period_duration` (String) The billing period, as an ISO 8601 duration, the user must currently be subscribed to. Left out, any billing period matches.
- `once_per_user` (Boolean) Whether a user who has ever had this offer can never have it again. Defaults to `false`.

<a id="nestedatt--targeting--upgrade_rule--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `targeting.upgrade_rule.scope`

Optional:

- `specific_subscription_in_app` (String) The product id of another subscription of the same app.
- `this_subscription` (Attributes) The subscription this offer belongs to: write `this_subscription = {}`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--targeting--upgrade_rule--scope--this_subscription))

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = googleplay_subscription_offer.pro_monthly_intro
  id = "com.example.app/pro_monthly/monthly/intro"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an offer by package name, product id, base plan id and offer id.
tofu import googleplay_subscription_offer.pro_monthly_intro com.example.app/pro_monthly/monthly/intro
```
